packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 17 - unverified image reading (blind; no identification was revealed to me in context)

NOTES AS I GO (survey and limitations at the end)

image-001.jpg (overview)
A book lying open/face down with its spine exposed (colour card and ruler at left; ruler runs bottom 0 to top 18 cm). The spine covering is lost; between the sewing stations, parchment spine-lining panels are visible. Two panels carry script, upright in the image:
 - upper panel (ruler c. 9.6-13.2 cm): 7 lines of a small, heavily abbreviated cursive hand in red-brown ink;
 - lower panel (ruler c. 5.5-8.8 cm): 4 lines of a larger, different hand (rounder, bolder letters), brown ink.
Panels above (c. 14-17 cm) and below (c. 1-5 cm) look blank or abraded. Lines are cut at both sides by the spine edges (c. 2.3 cm of width visible).

image-002.jpg (tile: upper panel)
Small cursive with many abbreviations (suspensions with flourished strokes, superscript letters). Dark stain at top centre. Each line cut left and right.
image-002 l.1: [...] p(ro)p(ter)(?) [..]c(?) [... stain ...] ɔ(?) s(u)b(stanti)a(?) [...] s[...]      (rubbed; a "p"-sign with crossed descender at left; "sba" with stroke = s(u)b(stanti)a?)
image-002 l.2: [...]u(?)[superscr.] p(ar)ti(?) sicut ad(?) l(?)iu[...]      (first group cut, minims with superscript sign; "paci"/"p(ar)ti"/"p(ri)ma" - p with stroke + 3 short letters; "sicut" clear; then "a" + tall looped letter(s) + "iu": "aliu(d)"/"album"/"ad lu")
image-002 l.3: [..] ac(?) ingit(ur)(?) p(ro)(?) n(on)(?) se(?)[...]      (letters as seen: "a c/r - m/in - i g i t" with a final flourish: "attingit", "ac tingit", "ar(guitur)..." all possible; then a crossed "p" sign (p(ro)/p(er)); "n" with stroke = n(on); then tall "s"/"f" + "e", cut)
image-002 l.4: [...]t(ur)(?) p(ro)(?) ul(?)[stroke] sig(nifica)re(?) ad[...]      (left word rubbed, ends in a flourish; crossed "p" sign again; "ul"/"ut"/"ill" with a stroke above (u(e)l? ill(u)d?); "s i g" with superscript "re"/"ie": sig(nifica)re / sig(ni)e?; "ad" + cut)
image-002 l.5: n(on)(?) s(ecundu)m(?) d(?)[superscr.] s(u)b(stanti)am inf[...]      (left edge "n" with stroke, above it another small "n"-like sign; a tall S-like letter + "em"/"cui" + tall s, with a superscript "d"-like sign with stroke above the middle - I cannot resolve this word; "sbam" with stroke = s(u)b(stanti)am fairly clear; "inf" + cut - cf. next lines)
image-002 l.6: [..] s(ed)(?) infinita(?) f(or)ma(?)[...]      (left: a tall letter with flourish + "s;"-like = s(ed)/s(cilicet)?; "mfıuıta" = "infinita" or "inferiora"; then "f" + minims "ma"/"inu" = f(or)ma?/finit-?, cut)
image-002 l.7: [...]t(ur)(?) actu inf(?) iute(?)[...]      (left word with flourish above; "actu" fairly clear with a stroke over the u = actu(m)?; "inf" with a long stroke = inf(initum)/inf(ra)?; then minims + "te"/"tc" with stroke, cut)

image-003.jpg (tile: lower panel)
Four widely spaced lines in a larger, rounder hand (uncial-like d, round letters, 3-shaped final sign), red-brown ink; clearly not the hand of the upper panel. Wide interline space, no gloss visible in it (a small dot above l.2; superscript "o" above the last word of l.3). Cut left and right.
image-003 l.1: [...]i(?)ꝫ ex l(?)ꝫ relig(?)[...]      (letters as seen: a minim + 3-shaped sign (= -et/-us/-que?) ; "e x"/"c x"; a tall letter + 3-shaped sign ("lꝫ"/"hꝫ"/"sꝫ" = l(icet)? h(abet)? s(ed)?); then "r e l i" + a descending letter (g/q), cut: "relig-"/"reliq-")
image-003 l.2: [tall stroke at edge] ozno(?) como(?)[...]      (letters as seen: "o", z-shaped round r, "n/u", "o" = "orno"/"oruo"; then "c o m o" or "co(n)no"/"corno" - the third letter group is 3 minims joined to a preceding "o/c"; a tall stroke begins at the right edge)
image-003 l.3: [...]s(?)atis(?) huic q(u)o(que)(?)      (first word cut at left: tall s/f + "a" + "t/c" + "i" + final round s/3-sign: "satis"/"facis"/"sacis"; "huic" clear; then "q" with superscript "o" and a 3-shaped sign = q(u)o(que)? q(uo)ꝫ)
image-003 l.4: [...]s(?) dicas g(?) l(?)[...]      (a small rubbed group with superscript at left; "dicas" clear (uncial d); then "g" or "q" with a mark, and a tall letter "l"/"b" + traces, cut and abraded)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
- Two parchment spine-lining panels in situ on an exposed spine; script upright in the supplied images; each panel is a horizontal slice c. 2.3 cm wide from a larger leaf, so no column edge, margin, heading or initial is visible. A tight view: the layout of the parent leaves cannot be inferred.
- The two panels are in two different hands and line spacings (upper: 7 lines in c. 3.5 cm, small abbreviated cursive; lower: 4 lines in c. 3.3 cm, large rounded hand). Observation: they look like pieces of two different manuscripts, or of text and something else on one leaf; I cannot tell which.
- No rubric, coloured initial, underlining, running title or marginal gloss visible on either. The wide spacing of the lower panel would leave room for interlinear glossing, but none is visible (tentative remark only).
- Tentative interpretation: the abbreviations in the upper panel (s(u)b(stanti)am, actu, infinit-(?), f(or)ma(?), sig(nifica)re(?), n(on), sicut) are of the kind used in scholastic prose; that is an inference from abbreviation habits, not an identification.

SELECTED SPANS / UNREAD
- I read all 7 lines of the upper panel (image-002) and all 4 of the lower (image-003); these are the only script-bearing areas supplied. No connected sentence is recoverable. Most secure words: upper "sicut" (l.2), "s(u)b(stanti)am" (l.5), "actu" (l.7); lower "huic" (l.3), "dicas" (l.4), "ex" (l.1).
- Unread/unresolved: the first word-group of most upper lines; upper l.1 (stained); the word after "n(on)" in upper l.5. The blank-looking panels at c. 14-17 cm and c. 1-5 cm on the ruler were not supplied as tiles; the overview shows no script on them.

LIMITATIONS
- Lines truncated on both sides by the spine width; the upper hand is very small and its suspensions are ambiguous without context, which I have deliberately not supplied. Expansions in parentheses are proposals only.
- A view with the lining lifted, or the reverse of the panels, and a slightly wider/raking tile of the upper panel's left edge would help.
- No identification was revealed to me in context and I did not attempt one. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files (the initial directory listing showed a packet.json that I did not open).
- This is an unverified image reading.
